text:
diane_customer: Hey team — started getting a bunch of support tickets from EU customers, p95 latency jumped to ~400-600ms. They say requests are being routed to us-east. I can repro from a browser in Frankfurt: curl shows X-Region: us-east and high RTT.

amanda_support: Sorry about that — can you paste a sample request-id and one or two IPs from the client side? Also a quick `dig` / `curl -v` output would help.

diane_customer: sample request-id: r-0a1b2c3d. Client IP (edge observed): 85.214.12.34. Here's quick dig and curl from my laptop in DE:

`$ dig +short app.example.com @8.8.8.8`
`34.200.11.45`

`$ curl -sv https://api.example.com/health -H 'X-Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d'`
`> < HTTP/2 200`
`< X-Region: us-east`
`< X-Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d`

rohan_eng: Thanks — that IP (34.200.11.45) is in our us-east anycast pool. Two quick hypotheses: 1) upstream GeoIP mapping returned wrong ASN/geo and DNS answered with a us-east-A record, or 2) EDNS/EDNS-client-subnet caused a wrong resolution upstream and the client's resolver cached it.

marta_prodops: Can you also run a traceroute and `dig +trace` from the client's location? Need to see if the authoritative returned a us-east answer or if a local resolver served a stale cached value.

diane_customer: traceroute attached (shortened):
`1  10.0.0.1`
`2  84.16.0.1`
`3  34.200.11.1`

`$ dig +trace app.example.com`
`;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR`
`;; AUTHORITY SECTION:`
`app.example.com. 300 IN A 34.200.11.45`

amanda_support: Ok we have enough to escalate. rohan / marta — can you check the edge logs for r-0a1b2c3d and the DNS responses for the authoritative nameservers at the timestamp (1762601123)? Also tell the customer short repro steps to verify after we push a mitigation.

rohan_eng: Pulling logs now — ingress shows request from 85.214.12.34 reached our frontdoor, but we routed it to backend pool us-east-1 due to the A record for app.example.com resolving to a us-east anycast IP. The resolver that answered at the time appears to be a corporate resolver that had cached an older answer. I suspect our GeoIP DB was out-of-date for a range and a previous deployment pinned that prefix to us-east in DNS.

geoip-bot: geoip-db-check: last-updated 2026-02-18T03:12:10Z, pending package 2026-02-25 ingest (outdated prefixes present).

marta_prodops: That bot lines up — we have a known lag on our automated GeoIP ingestion pipeline; the scheduled ingest failed last week and the follow-on step didn't error loudly. I can do a manual ingest and reload the DNS service. Mitigation options: reduce authoritative TTL to 60s, force a reload, update GeoIP DB, and add a temporary route rule to pin eu-west for known EU ASN ranges.

amanda_support: Diane — short repro steps we will ask you to run after we push the fixes so you can validate quickly:
1) `sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches` (or restart the resolver)
2) `dig +short app.example.com @8.8.8.8` and `dig +short app.example.com @1.1.1.1`
3) `curl -H 'X-Request-ID: test-123' -sv https://api.example.com/health` and check `X-Region` header

rohan_eng: I'm going to do a geoip DB manual ingest now, then reload dns and set TTL to 60 temporarily. I'll also push a canary rule to prefer eu-west for our EU ASN set to avoid broad disruption while caches clear.

geoip-bot: geoip-db-update: started by marta_prodops at 1762602000

marta_prodops: Manual ingest complete, dns daemon reloaded, authoritative TTL set to 60s. I also applied the temporary routing override for ASN ranges assigned to EU providers. Deploy id: deploy-geoip-1762602100. rohan — please monitor ingress for misrouted requests.

rohan_eng: Watching logs — I see new resolves returning eu-west IPs for several test resolvers. Also added a quick fallback: if request's GeoIP region is EU but selected pool != eu-west, prefer eu-west (short-term).

amanda_support: Diane — when you have a minute can you run the three repro steps I pasted? Should see X-Region change to eu-west and latency drop. If the local corporate resolver still caches the old answer, step1 (flush) or using 1.1.1.1 should show the new result.

diane_customer: Ran them now:
`$ dig +short app.example.com @8.8.8.8` -> `18.194.22.88`
`$ curl -sv https://api.example.com/health -H 'X-Request-ID: test-123'` -> `X-Region: eu-west`
Latency now p95 ~ 80-120ms, much better. Thanks.

amanda_support: Great — rohan/marta any remaining follow-ups?

rohan_eng: Follow-ups: 1) fix GeoIP ingestion pipeline to surface failures (alerts), 2) roll back temp ASN override once we confirm stable, 3) backfill authoritative DNS with the corrected mapping and increase TTL back to 300 after 24h. I filed infra ticket INFRA-4523 and added steps to the runbook.

marta_prodops: I'll schedule the ingestion fix and alerting for tomorrow, and keep the temporary rule for 12h. Will also coordinate a controlled TTL increase.

amanda_support: Diane — marking this as resolved for now. If you or customers see any reoccurence paste a sample request-id and we'll reopen immediately. :thumbsup:

diane_customer: Thanks everyone, appreciate the fast response — will let you know if anything else pops up.

geoip-bot: geoip-db-update: completed successfully at 1762602300 (updated 12 prefixes, removed 3 stale mappings)

amanda_support: Closing thread.
